turns.prompt_text: What is the difference between ps4, ps4 slim, and ps4 pro?
turns.response_html:
The main differences between the original PlayStation 4, PS4 Slim, and PS4 Pro come down to physical size, power efficiency, processing performance, and resolution output. While all three models play the exact same library of PS4 games, they handle them differently.

Here is a direct comparison of how the three hardware models differ across their key specifications:

Key Takeaways

  • Original PS4 vs. PS4 Slim: Internally, these two deliver the exact same gaming performance and frame rates. The Sony PlayStation 4 Slim is simply a hardware refresh that runs noticeably quieter, cooler, and draws roughly 30% less power. However, Sony did remove the digital optical audio port on the Slim model.
  • PS4 Pro Upgrades: The Sony PlayStation 4 Pro is a high-end tier designed for 4K TVs. It features more than double the graphics processing power and a faster clock speed. This extra power enables 4K resolution upscaling, smoother and more stable frame rates (with some games hitting 60 FPS), better draw distances, and enhanced performance for PlayStation VR. It also adds a third USB port on the back, which is highly useful for connecting VR hardware or external storage.

Which One Should You Choose?

If you are gaming on a standard 1080p monitor or television and want a reliable, energy-efficient setup that doesn't take up much space, the PS4 Slim is the most practical choice. If you own a 4K display, want the highest visual fidelity, or intend to use PlayStation VR, the PS4 Pro provides a much smoother and sharper experience.
